item: Writer jobs notice a stop within the shutdown deadline (R689 (1))
summary: The summary/translation queue looked at its stop only after a whole generation (minutes on a CPU model), so the shutdown's 5 s stop_all_jobs gave up on it and disposed the engine under a writer: a queued run now waits on its generation in a side thread and looks at the stop every 0.2 s, so a stop ends the run at once (shutdown or Free the GPU: paused, the article in flight dropped and redone on resume; task-manager Stop: cancelled), and nothing the abandoned generation returns is stored; the abandoned batch makes no further model call (a long article stops after the part in flight), its side thread never opens the settings store, Free the GPU / Stop Ollama wait for that last call to return (R669 kept) and the next queued run starts only after it. The Insights backlog looked at its stop only between 300-article batches: now before each article. Also Lane F review rows 11 (a resumed translation skips only results in its own target; a summary keeps matching any prompt version, since an exact match would store the run's own summaries twice after a prompt or app change), 13 (a queue kick never blocks a request), 15 (the task-manager row shows a model name only when it is a closed name) and closed-set reasons for a failed Free the GPU / Stop Ollama / Ollama launch; a kick retry never starts a drain after the shutdown's stop. The disposal side (R689 (2)) is the data durability lane's src/database/after_shutdown.py. Tests: tests/test_shutdown_stop_deadline.py.
